correctness.rationale: An independent real-variable check uses D_b g(x)=g({bx}) and its Lebesgue adjoint B_b, the uniform inverse-branch average, with B_b f=f/b for f(x)=x-1/2. Both Markov actions preserve Lebesgue integrals. In B_M D_N the branch residues are Nj+floor(Nx) modulo M; when M,N are coprime they permute the M residues, yielding D_N B_M. Adjointness then gives <f,D_N^j B_M^l f>=1/(12 N^j M^l) and commuting-binomial expansion gives the all-lag law and its convergent sum. At lag two the reverse-order mixed term is <D_M f,D_N f>. Write M=dM', N=dN' and use uniformity of {dx}; the mixed integral reduces to coprime bases M',N', for which the same adjoint and permutation identities (also valid for base 1) give 1/(12 M'N')=d²/(12MN). The other mixed term is 1/(12MN). The stated C0,C1,C2 and lag-two defect follow, strictly positive exactly for d>1 when pq>0. The formula is algebraic in p and holds at the stated zero-Lyapunov parameter. Homburg–Kalle Theorem 1.1(ii) verifies the accompanying common-noise intermittency at zero exponent for these probabilities, with the exception for coalesced pairs; it is not a statement about this annealed covariance.
residual_risks: The checker swaps the names of the two positional base arguments versus the text; its matched formula uses the same swap and its samples include both orders, so this is not a mathematical discrepancy.
The p=0 dynamics can still randomly choose a branch; what is deterministic at that endpoint is the choice of contracting versus expanding type. The equivalence excludes both endpoints.

value.rationale: The natural stationary coordinate detects a structural arithmetic boundary: the entire covariance sequence is geometric exactly when a single lag-two equality holds. The excess gives its exact deviation for every pair of noncoprime bases. It also distinguishes geometric coordinate correlation at the critical probability from intermittency of common-noise pair dynamics; that coexistence is an interpretation, not an originality claim about intermittency itself.
residual_risks: The test is for the specified coordinate and stationary annealed law. It says nothing about a general observable's decay rate, a full operator mixing spectrum or quenched correlations.
